releases.legal_basis: Informed Patient consent to permit the receipt, processing and release of data by the HSCIC and for the release of ONS mortality data

texts.0d19c5c9ae5c: Objective for processing: The United Kingdom Immune Thrombocytopenia (UK ITP) Registry is a UK-wide registry of patients with the rare bleeding disorder ITP. Patients are enrolled when they are referred for ITP management at the Royal London Hospital or at any of its 60 participating referral centres nationwide. The Registry need to update its participants’ records on comorbid conditions, treatment, hospitalisation, outpatient appointments and mortality (including causes). Through population mobility or other reasons patients may receive care at other NHS institutions which are not covered by the Registry’s centres or certain study-related data may not have been captured through routine data collection for various reasons. The registry also has enrolees registered through centres which are no longer collaborating due to lack of resources. It is therefore important for the Registry to also engage the service of the HSCIC and ONS in order to consolidate and update its current data and also ensure data completeness and minimise loss to follow up. The registry will use the HSCIC services to: 1. ensure that our data remain complete and up-to-date 2. minimise lost to follow up 3. establish end of follow up for certain patients (i.e. when exited the cohort for any reason) 4. obtain study-related data which were previously time-consuming or challenging to collect 5. all-cause and cause-specific mortality are important outcomes to be included within the Registry studies Processing activities: We will use the data that you provide for analytical purposes as per study protocol. The data that we obtain from the HSCIC and ONS will be integrated with the overall data of the Registry. This will consolidate the existing data to fill in missing values wherever applicable, validate certain data we collect and vice versa, and obtain long term follow up data (on several outcomes of interest) on patients with ITP. The analysis will be conducted in multiple parts and will involve various analytical techniques from summary statistic to multivariate regression analysis (including survival analysis techniques). We aim to identify, wherever possible factors that heighten or reduce risk of certain outcomes, such as thromboembolism, bleeding and mortality. The findings. All data that we process during the analytical phase will be fully anonymised and no reports of the findings will contain identifiable information. All findings will be disseminated to the general public via peer review journals and the Registry’s newsletter. Updated contact details on our participants and general practitioners may be used to contact them as per study requirements, especially for operational activities. Specific outputs expected, including target date: • Estimate ITP incidence, prevalence, mortality rate and survival rate • Description of baseline demographic and clinical characteristics of our ITP cohort • Description of disease progression over time (platelet counts, bleeding episodes, severity, comorbid events, hospitalisation, etc.) • Prevalence of risk factors for thromboembolic events (TE) and bleeding events • Incidence of TEs (e.g. stratified analysis by comorbidities, treatment, etc.) • Mortality rate stratified by certain characteristics and description of common causes of death Description of current treatment paradigm and their effectiveness in terms of certain patient-reported outcomes, clinically relevant outcomes and mortality. The study is to conclude in May 2017. Expected measurable benefits to health and/or social care including target date: • better data quality which in turn lead to robust and reliable findings to assist clinical, policy and regulatory decision making • provision of certain data via HSCIC will allow us to channel current resources to collect specific ITP-related data from medical records • need to deliver our reports as soon as possible to the ITP community and regulators • address a need for evidence on the epidemiology of ITP for the UK (e.g. prevalence, incidence, survival and mortality) using a real-life disease-based Registry Provide evidence on treatment effectiveness which is currently in great demand
